title: Data-driven model reveals increased stability of CAG-expanded huntingtin RNA due to MID1 binding
authors: Yuhong Liu; Annika Reisbitzer; Domagoj Dorešić; Jan Hasenauer; Sybille Krauß; Tatjana Tchumatchenko
one_liner_zh: 该文构建数据驱动模型研究MID1蛋白与huntingtin RNA结合对RNA稳定性的影响，虽涉及蛋白-RNA互作，但对象为RNA结合蛋白而非TF-DNA体系，且方法为数据驱动建模而非AI或物理模拟，与课题关联度较低。
abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBP) are important regulators of RNA metabolism. In neurode-generative disorders such as Huntington’s Disease (HD), disrupted RBP-RNA interactions contribute to neuronal dysfunction. One such RBP, Midline 1 (MID1), has been shown to aberrantly associate with mutant huntingtin ( Htt ) RNA, enhancing its translation, yet the mechanism driving this effect remains unknown. Here, we develop a computational model to understand the role of MID1. Based on previously published data, our model predicts that MID1 increases the stability of the Htt RNA. We experimentally validate this prediction, showing that overexpression of MID1 significantly prolongs the half-life of mutant Htt RNA. Furthermore, we evaluate model refinements, including clustering of MID1-bound RNA, which allow capturing all key observations in the data. Together, we provide a data-driven framework that underlines the importance of RBP-RNA interaction in post-transcriptional regulation. This framework also shows how individual molecular reactions jointly determine RNA stability and protein levels in HD.
abstract_zh: RNA结合蛋白（RBP）是RNA代谢的重要调控因子。在诸如亨廷顿病（HD）等神经退行性疾病中，RBP-RNA相互作用的紊乱会导致神经元功能障碍。其中一种RBP，即中线1（MID1），已被证明异常地与突变型亨廷顿蛋白（Htt）RNA结合，增强其翻译，但驱动这一效应的机制仍未知。在此，我们开发了一个计算模型来理解MID1的作用。基于先前发表的数据，我们的模型预测MID1会增加Htt RNA的稳定性。我们通过实验验证了这一预测，表明MID1的过表达显著延长了突变型Htt RNA的半衰期。此外，我们评估了模型改进，包括MID1结合RNA的聚类，这些改进能够捕捉数据中的所有关键观察结果。综合来看，我们提供了一个数据驱动的框架，强调了RBP-RNA相互作用在转录后调控中的重要性。该框架还展示了单个分子反应如何共同决定HD中的RNA稳定性和蛋白质水平。
